en: When you turn back this way,
Where Ken-Kol pours its waters in,
At the eastern edge of Talas,
My son, on the hills the horses had pied heads;
Behind your father, you, his son, were still young.
Unable to collect myself,
My widowed self was in distress.
I had no swift steed to catch and ride;
Then I had no kinsman to rely upon.
Vast Talas was no land for me;
Those Kyrgyz were no people of mine.
Deceit lay in their words;
If they could, they meant to bring me down.
They meant to dig my pit;
If they could, they meant to boil misery for me.
They meant to bring upon my head
A horror no human should see!
Left behind at his head,
I became the blood-shedding hero's widow
At the age of thirty-two.
'God who strikes will utterly
Strike me,' I kept thinking.
One onslaught upon my head—
'He will bring it down,' I kept thinking.
When they plundered my treasury,
When they joined to bring me down,
'Tomorrow, when the orphan grows
And returns to his people,
He will be left powerless,' I thought.
'With all the treasury gone,
He will be left without livestock,' I thought.
My heart was sorely torn;
Tears poured from my eyes.
'They will join to bring me down,' I thought.
'If the six villains wish,
This treasury of mine
They will utterly destroy,' I thought.
'They will take the measure of my strength,' I thought,
'And ruin my treasury,' I thought.
Without letting one person know,
Without letting anyone suspect,
I shouted in my wrath
And summoned five champions.
I gave horses as their payment;
I promptly paid each day's wages.
'So they dig well without turning aside,' I thought,
And gave gold and jewels by the pood.
In a blue cliff veiled in gray mist,
In a blue mountain standing still,
Leaving it alone by day,
By night I dug the cave.
Never giving up hope,
I dug the cave each day.
I had its mouth contrived
So that only one person could fit.
I had the space beyond dug out
So that six thousand sheep could lie there.
Giving sharp iron crowbars,
I had the cave's interior hollowed out.
I had it made exceedingly splendid.
I had seventy gelded camels fitted with pack saddles;
The sand taken from within,
I had poured into the broad waters of Talas.
With the labor of seventy gelded camels,
For seven nights I had loads carried without rest;
Your father's treasury
I had gathered into that cave.
I sealed its mouth with glue;
I had it contrived in a wondrous way.
'So no sign remains,' I thought,
And the dark sand above
I had brought down over the treasury's mouth.
One day as I lay thinking,
Allah's sun grew overcast in the sky;
Upon my widowed head,
Sixty worries came at once:
'When I leave Talas,
If those five wretches wish,
Will they join to bring me down?
Digging my pit deep,
Together boiling misery for me,
Telling someone else,
Will they open my treasury?
Turning witnesses before others,
Loose tongues exposing my deed,
Will they ruin my possessions
And put an end to my laughter?'
Harboring mistrust of the champions,
Unable to trust any man,
As dusk came and the sun set,
As the first of the people lay still,
I shouted in anger.
'Come here,' I myself said,
And summoned the five champions.
I gave poison measured in a ladle;
I gave water with a spoon.
I loaded my cartridge pouch and fired,
I made them all cry, 'My belly!'
Thus I fed them their allotted portion
And removed the five champions from this world.
For the sake of that mournful place,
And also for the sake of your treasure,
I slaughtered the five champions.
Beside the hearth,
I folded them at the waist
And buried them without a trace.
There is still more I must tell:
I killed them though they had committed no crime;
Upon my neck, your wretched mother's,
Lies the blood of those five champions.
Your wretched mother that I am
Has an endless tale to tell.
When the dawn of Judgment comes,
For those five innocent champions
I may well become a black donkey.
Saddle your horse properly and go;
For those five innocent champions
Recite the Quran with care!
Let me leave your treasure aside.
Now listen, my son;
Let me begin with what followed:
In the valley of broad Talas,
Beside the mouth of Ken-Kol,
On the spur where the mountain ends,
At the projecting headland,
At the edge of great Ak-Chiy,
Upon the main road,
Thinking, 'God will take your khan father Manas,
That mighty conqueror, that beloved lion;
When I leave Talas,
No trace of the sultan will remain,
And his whereabouts will be unknown,'
I had seven hundred gelded camels pack-saddled;
I had their sacks and ropes put right.
I gathered those who knew the land
And sent them searching through the world.
Beyond Andijan,
On this side of Amangen,
Under the wing of the khan of Kokon,
Kuleshen and Chiymaydam:
I had both places shown together.
The refractory clay of Kuleshen—
I had that refractory clay brought.
Seven hundred gelded camels carried loads;
I had its earth brought here.
I had it mixed in a great vat;
Chopping up cow and goat hair,
I had it added to that mud.
I brought it to the proper kneaded state
And had horsehair sprinkled over it.
The son of Aksakalbai,
The mighty Sart Aralbai,
And sixty mighty men with hoes:
I had them tread the clay thoroughly.
I levied a tribute on the Argyn
And gathered six thousand goat wethers.
Slaughtering all six thousand goat wethers,
I fired bricks and built it strong.
Your father's mausoleum
Until six ages had passed away,
I built it to stand unbroken.
I did not sit looking on idly;
Levying tribute on the Kyrgyz,
I gathered seven thousand goat wethers.
Slaughtering all seven thousand goat wethers,
I fired bricks and built it strong.
Until seven ages had passed away,
My accomplished one's mausoleum,
I built it to stand unbroken.
To the scribe in Mecca
I gave six swift horses;
Saying, 'Let him come to us at once,'
I sent a letter the size of a palm.
I had great Mecca searched
And had the great ishan brought.
'When my orphan grows to maturity
And joins the ranks himself,
When he moves back to Talas,
While he recites the Quran
For his departed father Manas,
Let him see what happened here,' I thought,
And had it made a wonder.
The seething tumult of that great upheaval,
The clash with Kakanchy,
The assault on Great Beijing:
I pictured them all together.
Flowing across the face of the earth,
I pictured the blood.
Lying crooked in death,
I pictured the fallen souls.
With their great teeth jutting out,
The horse corpses piled like mountains:
I pictured them too.
With their mustaches bristling,
The warrior corpses piled like mountains:
Hey, I pictured that too.
Infidel and Muslim:
I pictured their clash.
Fighting without retreat,
I pictured their battle.
The two khans Baakybai and Duulat:
I pictured those khans.
Khan Alooke and Khan Azyz:
I pictured those warriors.
The horse I rode was Arbuudan;
My own great dark figure—
I pictured myself as well.
Concerned with nothing else,
You struggled for my breast;
The dark blood running down my face
Poured down your temples:
My foal, I pictured you too.
'If he survives, my only one
Will come to this Talas,' I thought.
'This white mausoleum standing here:
If my foal enters within,
He will see what happened,' I thought.
When you enter through the doorway,
If you look to your left,
Jerking on a golden lead rope,
Struggling upon Algara,
As though his wife were seized by a birth demon,
As though pursuers were close behind,
As though his wife had borne a son,
The frenzied warrior Kalcha:
I set him astride Alkara
And pictured him too.
Great boots stretch out upon his feet;
His neck cranes like a rooster's.
His spectacles gleam;
When you look at Konurbai,
A coral stone the size of a leather flask
Hey, flashes upon his crown.
A lacquered pipe with a golden stem;
Kalcha as great as a shelter:
A warrior skilled among spearmen,
An outstanding hero who knows the enemy's ways.
Look carefully and you will see:
His bristling mustache,
Like the handle of a greased axe;
His dangling nose,
Like the sheath of a long straight sword;
The corners of his two eyes,
Like an open grave;
The space between his brows,
Like a rich man's broad summer pasture.
Konurbai, who speared your father Manas:
He is that lion sustained by Shai;
He is that warrior who knows the enemy's ways.
The black horse beneath him—
I wonder whether his black horse
Has wings upon its flanks.
Whenever it may be, Konurbai:
Let twelve worlds come against him together,
He is used to grinding them like roasted grain.
